objective: Deliver a credential-free We Remember hackathon Fixture MVP that proves consented private sharing, persisted five-stage responsibility, blocked two-party handover, and atomic owner and reminder transfer
constraints: This Run is a local fictional Fixture demo and must not require credentials, external model calls, production identity, public deployment, or private real-world data.
The four first-wave tasks run in isolated worktrees from the same accepted base and must not reuse or cherry-pick any failed Attempt.
Private Fixture messages remain self-only until explicit same-speaker consent; authorization, consent, handover, reporting, and persistence are deterministic.
Unsupported free-form or live-provider behavior fails closed and is post-MVP rather than being simulated as production-ready.
The accepted HAND-001 SHA is reused exactly; this Run does not rebuild the handover state machine.
Complete Unicode, sub-millisecond time, care, deletion/export, exhaustive failure, full visual-matrix, live-model, deployment, and release gates remain post-MVP.
Fixture, Local Demo, Public Runtime, Deployment, Release, and Official Acceptance evidence levels must never be conflated.

waves.description: Build the four smallest independent product slices needed by the core hackathon journey.

tasks.title: Build fixture-only private sharing and consent
tasks.spec: Implement a fresh credential-free Fixture flow through public module ports: create one self-only private message, produce a bounded deterministic signal draft, and let only the same active speaker explicitly share it to an allowed visibility. Do not call an external provider or accept caller-controlled prompt metadata. Unsupported free-form provider behavior must return blocked or needs_human_review. Recheck actor, space, evidence ownership, consent, and visibility before the shared write. Keep raw private content out of shared rows, reports, logs, and errors.
acceptance: The task starts from exact accepted base 217d9a3b421e8eef628483f349346eea981a435c and contains no failed Attempt ancestor
The canonical fictional private message produces a deterministic bounded draft through public conversation ports without network access or credentials
Before explicit same-speaker sharing, shared signal count remains zero
Discard, missing consent, inactive actor, wrong actor, or wrong space returns denied or blocked and persists zero shared writes
Successful consent creates one visibility-scoped derived signal with provenance but no raw private content
Duplicate confirmation creates at most one shared signal
Logs and errors contain identifiers and outcomes only

tasks.title: Build persisted five-stage responsibility reporting
tasks.spec: Implement a fresh deterministic responsibility capability through public module ports. Consume only consented shared signals, create the canonical Fixture responsibility domain and task, persist discoveredBy, deadlineKeptBy, scheduledBy, executedBy, and followedUpBy as first-class values, and generate a neutral report directly from those facts. Do not use an LLM for the MVP report or infer ownership from prose at report time. Exclude discussion-only, missing-evidence, denied, and needs-review inputs.
acceptance: The task starts from exact accepted base 217d9a3b421e8eef628483f349346eea981a435c and contains no failed Attempt ancestor
The canonical consented signal creates one Fixture responsibility domain and task through public ports
All five responsibility-stage owners are explicit persisted command data rather than report-time inference
The report is deterministic, neutral, and contains no blame, score, ranking, diagnosis, or model-generated narrative
Discussion-only, missing-evidence, denied, and needs-review inputs do not appear in the report
Invalid actor, space, or source data yields zero responsibility or report mutation

tasks.title: Build the core three-role Fixture experience
tasks.spec: Build a Chinese Web Fixture experience against a typed local client seam. Cover only the core journey: the older subject's mobile private-message share decision, the primary carer's neutral five-stage report and blocked handover, the partner's confirmation, and the final visible reduction of the primary carer's burden after transfer. Keep the interface warm, restrained, and role-specific. Show Fixture, Local Demo, and Not Production Acceptance labels persistently. Do not add live authentication, external model calls, broad settings, care, deletion, export, or nonessential animation.
acceptance: The subject can complete the canonical share decision at 390x844 with one visible primary action
The primary and partner desktop views show the report, blocked reason, each confirmation, and final owner and reminder change at 1440x900
The demo's primary actions have no blocking overlap, clipping, or hidden text at the two target viewports
The typed client seam supports loading, the core success path, and one recoverable integration error without embedding backend logic
Fixture, Local Demo, and Not Production Acceptance labels remain visible on every core screen
UI copy is Chinese, neutral, non-diagnostic, and contains no production-auth or live-data claim

tasks.title: Create the canonical core Fixture and focused acceptance
tasks.spec: Create one canonical fictional three-role Fixture graph for the core journey and focused Playwright acceptance tagged @mvp-core. The Fixture contains one private message, one consented derived signal, one responsibility domain with all five stage owners, one handover blocked by missing information, two confirmations, and one future reminder that moves with the owner. Author one happy-path browser specification plus no-consent, blocked, and one-sided-confirmation negative cases. The tests may target the documented integration seam and are executed only after MVP-INT-001 merges the product slices.
acceptance: All people, messages, identifiers, health references, and events are visibly fictional and internally consistent
One canonical graph is the sole source for UI, module, database, and browser Fixture values
The @mvp-core happy path covers consent, report, blocked handover, both confirmations, owner and reminder transfer, and reload persistence
Focused negative cases prove no-consent yields zero shared writes, blocked handover leaves owner unchanged, and one-sided confirmation cannot accept
Browser assertions require persistent Fixture, Local Demo, and Not Production Acceptance labels
The worker check validates Fixture structure and testkit behavior without requiring unfinished integration routes

waves.description: Merge the four accepted product slices and accepted handover capability into one real local Fixture application.

tasks.title: Integrate the real core Fixture journey
tasks.spec: Start from exact base 217d9a3b421e8eef628483f349346eea981a435c. Fetch and cleanly merge --no-ff the exact accepted remote SHAs for MVP-CONV-001, MVP-RESP-001, MVP-EXPR-001, MVP-QA-001, and accepted HAND-001 SHA 59e4bcb98be9d21432a92d02e7d01962bc4451cb. Abort on conflict or unexpected ancestry. Add only integration-owned Fixture session, public command/query composition, database adapters, routes, and demo documentation. Wire the canonical journey through the real Next.js UI, public handlers, and PostgreSQL. Keep provider behavior deterministic and credential-free. Do not patch product modules sideways or claim production readiness.
acceptance: Each accepted product SHA and HAND-001 is an exact second parent of a clean no-ff merge and no failed Attempt is an ancestor
The canonical private message has zero shared rows before consent and creates one derived shared signal after same-speaker consent
The report reads the persisted five-stage fields through real query handlers
Missing information and one-sided confirmation keep the handover blocked with owner and reminder unchanged
After both confirmations, owner and future reminder move atomically and both role views retain the new state after reload
The flow runs through the real Next.js runtime and disposable PostgreSQL rather than disconnected static mocks
Fixture, Local Demo, and Not Production Acceptance labels remain visible and documentation makes no live-model, production-auth, deployment, release, or official-acceptance claim
No-consent, blocked, and one-sided negative browser cases pass with zero forbidden mutation
